evidence:
Inventory: 2 zero-weight gates, 43 functional binary criteria, 5 polish binary, 5 visual likert. Pairwise review of all scored criteria against the shared protocols S/M/L/C/B/N/T/U/K/R/V/A/D (functional/prompt.md:25-49). Most rows are well separated: role rows split by actor (hro_mgr_late_stages / hro_mgr_early_refused / hro_mgr_other_job / hro_observer_readonly / hro_candidate_no_staff / hro_anonymous), capacity split by path (hro_interview_full single, hro_bulk_places set, hro_undo_full undo), undo split by outcome (restores / conflict / once), and polish explicitly hands scrolled-up arrival to Functional ('This row owns the draft and focus; where the view goes while reading earlier messages is graded in Functional', polish/judge.toml:32). Visual prompt guards double deduction ('Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row', visual/prompt.md:14). Gates carry 0.0 weight (scoring.toml) so gate/scored overlap is not double reward. No pair demands incompatible products: Enter sends (hro_msg_compose) vs Enter after session end prompts sign-in (hro_pol_session_resume) is consistent with rules 6 Drafts; per-user drafts satisfy both hro_drafts reload persistence and 'Mei sees no draft'; 'box empty after send' vs 'failed send stays in box' are compatible.

CONFIRMED DUPLICATE (defect): hro_arrive_bottom (functional/judge.toml:59-66, weight 1) second leg 'and the three cards moved together land below V' grades exactly the same observable as hro_bulk_move (functional/judge.toml:203-210, weight 1.5) 'three selected cards move to one stage in one action and arrive at the bottom of that stage in their board order'. Both are observed at the single protocol step B(3) 'Select Y, W and X ... move them to Screen together: they arrive below V as W, X, Y' (functional/prompt.md:33). hro_bulk_move's bar strictly contains that leg (bottom AND board order AND all-in-one-action), so hro_arrive_bottom's second leg is subsumed. The functional prompt has no 'do not deduct the same defect twice' guard (unlike visual/prompt.md:14); its line 13 'score EACH criterion independently' makes the judge apply both. The internal workbook annotation for this row (retest once within a flow, not again separately) and REVIEW_POLICY 'scoring distinct promises separately' both point the same way. The single-card leg of hro_arrive_bottom (B lands below A, prompt M) is a distinct observable and is fine on its own.

Lesser overlaps (Note-level, recorded for reconciliation, not independently blocking): (a) hro_candidate_view (judge.toml:379-381) leg 'they can read and reply in their own conversations' overlaps hro_msg_exchange (judge.toml:298-300) 'Tomas ... read it and reply' - a candidate whose reply cannot be sent fails both. (b) hro_msg_compose 'afterwards the box is empty' vs hro_drafts 'Fails if a draft ... survives sending' - an app that does not clear the box after send can be failed by both. (c) hro_interview_full 'that card stays where it was' vs hro_refused_put_back 'card is shown back in its real stage and place' - the fail clause of hro_interview_full ('Interview can hold more cards than places') keeps it server-scoped, so this is a dependency rather than duplication. (d) hro_pol_live_board / hro_pol_live_thread score 0 when the live update never arrives, which also costs hro_live_board / hro_msg_exchange; this is a required positive-control dependency per REVIEW_POLICY ('A dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing'), not duplication. (e) hro_arrive_bottom's generic fail clause 'an arriving card is placed anywhere but the bottom' could be misread against hro_undo_restores (undo returns V to the top of Applied, rules 3 Undo); the leg list scopes it, so P3 latent ambiguity only. Out-of-scope observation for the owner (rows 33/48): hro_unread_counts (judge.toml:334-336) says Tomas's two new messages land on 'Tomas Varga's Data Analyst conversation' (seeded JOB-DATA, seed_data.json:93) while protocol U (prompt.md:39) sends them 'On Tomas's conversation from T' (the new J2 conversation); this is a criterion/protocol target mismatch, not an incompatible-product demand.

No runtime evidence is needed to establish source-level duplication; none was run.
counterexample: Broken app: bulk move is atomic and keeps board order but inserts the moved set at the TOP of the destination stage (above V); single-card moves correctly land at the bottom. Protocol B(3) shows W, X, Y above V. hro_bulk_move fails ('arrive at the bottom of that stage') AND hro_arrive_bottom fails ('the three cards moved together land below V'), so one defect costs weight 2.5 instead of 1.5. Conversely, an app that only gets bulk arrival right cannot earn hro_arrive_bottom without also passing the same observation already credited by hro_bulk_move, so the two rows do not discriminate independent promises.
suggested_fix: Remove the second leg from hro_arrive_bottom so it grades only single-card arrival at the bottom (e.g. 'B, moved into a Screen that already holds A, lands below A; a card moved forward into a non-empty stage lands at its bottom'), leaving bulk arrival position solely to hro_bulk_move; optionally add a functional-prompt line forbidding deduction of one observed defect in more than one row.
